content.introduction: Real GDP grew at an annual rate of 1.4% in Q4 2025. The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis released this advance estimate. The increase was driven by consumer spending and investment.
body: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 1.4 percent in the fourth quarter of 2025 (October, November, and December)
Schedule update: GDP (Advance Estimate), 4th Quarter and Year 2025, and Personal Income and Outlays, December 2025, will be released on Feb. 20

[](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-advance-estimate-4th-quarter-and-year-2025). *   [News Release](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-advance-estimate-4th-quarter-and-year-2025#home). *   [Related Materials](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-advance-estimate-4th-quarter-and-year-2025#menu1). *   [Contacts](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-advance-estimate-4th-quarter-and-year-2025#menu2). **Real gross domestic product** (GDP) [increased at an annual rate of 1.4 percent](https://apps.bea.gov/iTable/?reqid=19&step=2&isuri=1&categories=survey#eyJhcHBpZCI6MTksInN0ZXBzIjpbMSwyLDNdLCJkYXRhIjpbWyJjYXRlZ29yaWVzIiwiU3VydmV5Il0sWyJOSVBBX1RhYmxlX0xpc3QiLCIxIl1dfQ==) in the fourth quarter of 2025 (October, November, and December), according to the advance estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis. The [contributors to the increase in real GDP](https://apps.bea.gov/iTable/?reqid=19&step=2&isuri=1&categories=survey#eyJhcHBpZCI6MTksInN0ZXBzIjpbMSwyLDNdLCJkYXRhIjpbWyJjYXRlZ29yaWVzIiwiU3VydmV5Il0sWyJOSVBBX1RhYmxlX0xpc3QiLCIzMiJdXX0=) in the fourth quarter were increases in consumer spending and investment. For more information, refer to the "[Technical Notes](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-advance-estimate-4th-quarter-and-year-2025#TechNote)" below. (Refer to “[Technical Notes](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-advance-estimate-4th-quarter-and-year-2025#TechNote)” below for information on how BEA imputed missing Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) October prices.). The news release text has been modified to include links to BEA’s online [Interactive Data Tables](https://www.bea.gov/itable/national-gdp-and-personal-income). Real GDP increased at an annual rate of 1.4 percent (0.4 percent at a quarterly rate [1](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-advance-estimate-4th-quarter-and-year-2025#_ftn1)) in the fourth quarter, reflecting increases in consumer spending and investment that were partly offset by decreases in government spending and exports.
